dossier.public_summary: The 4 dips look flat but their depths do not match: odd transits are much shallower than even ones and the drafts are all over the place, dominating the signal. That pattern and the extra dip 21% as deep as the main one match a stellar binary folded at half its period, not a 3-earth-radius planet on the star. The centroid is inconclusive so the blend cannot be fully excluded, but the target is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ strongly at 7.3σ with a depth ratio 3.5 and same-sign excess, with the two deepest events dominating the signal. This is positive evidence for a binary at twice the 12.4-d period, not a nearly 3-Rearth planet, despite the flat shape (shape.v_sigma=-1.828).

reasons.why: Depths are even more inconsistent within the single sector than the odd/even average suggests, p~2.3e-12. Two bad/shallow events and two deep events produced the 13.36 SNR; removing one changes the depth dramatically.

reasons.why: No on-target centroid confirmation and the very low planet_rank (~0.1, only one planet in ten scores this low) support that the inconsistent eclipses are not a diluted planet on the target. The 22% secondary dip is above the achromatic brightening noise and consistent with stellar eclipses rather than a planetary secondary.
